questions.question:
In the following sentence, four words or phrases have been underlined. One of them is incorrect. Choose the INCORRECT word or phrase from the given options.

American officials says this is due to a lack of transparency surrounding the virus in China
questions.solution:
The phrase in option (d) is incorrect. According to the subject-verb agreement rule, we cannot use the singular verb 'says' with the plural subject 'officials'. Therefore, 'says' should be replaced with 'say' [plural verb] to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.question:
In the given sentence, several segments have been underlined. One of these underlined segments is grammatically incorrect in the context of its usage in the sentence. Identify the incorrect segment from the following options.

Neither Ketan nor his brother have attended the family gathering, as both are occupied with prior commitments and engagements elsewhere.
options: as both are occupied with prior
questions.solution:
The subject "Neither Ketan nor his brother" is singular, so the correct verb form should be "has attended." We use a singular verb when the subject after "nor" is singular and a plural verb when the subject after "nor" is plural. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The final correct sentence would be: Neither Ketan nor his brother has attended the family gathering, as both are occupied with prior commitments and engagements elsewhere.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.

I have always believed that kindness and empathy (has the power) to create positive change in the world, fostering connections that transcend differences.
questions.solution:
In this sentence, the subject is the compound noun phrase "kindness and empathy," which is plural. Therefore, the correct form of the verb "have" (plural) should be used to maintain subject-verb agreement. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Option (a) is incorrect as the singular verb 'is' cannot be used for the plural noun.

Option (c) is incorrect as 'are the power' puts the sentence in active voice and implies that 'kindness and empathy' are the doers of the action which is not exactly the case here. We require 'have' here to denote possession.

Option (d) is incorrect as 'having' would require a helping verb before it which is absent in the given sentence.

The corrected sentence: I have always believed that kindness and empathy have the power to create positive change in the world, fostering connections that transcend differences.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Voice refers to the form of a verb that indicates when a grammatical subject performs the action or is the receiver of the action. When a sentence is written in the active voice, the subject performs the action; in the passive voice, the subject receives the action.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Collaboration and teamwork is crucial for achieving success in any project.
questions.solution:
The part that contains the error is 'is'. The subject of the sentence is "Collaboration and teamwork," which is a compound subject joined by "and." Therefore, it is plural and requires the plural verb "are," not the singular verb "is." Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Collaboration and teamwork are crucial for achieving success in any project.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The quietest member of your family has a truly brilliant idea.
This responsibility place a particular burden on two men.
The products we source from them is not connected to the livestock industry.
It take courage to open yourself up to scrutiny again.
questions.solution:
The sentence given in option (a) is grammatically correct.

Option (b) is not correct. The error is related to the subject-verb agreement issue. The verb "place" (plural) is incorrect. The subject "This responsibility" is singular, so the verb should also be singular. "Places" is the correct third-person singular form of the verb "place."

The correct form should be "places" to agree with the subject "This responsibility," which is singular. The correct sentence is: This responsibility places a particular burden on two men.

Option (c) is incorrect. The error is related to the subject-verb agreement issue. The verb "is" is incorrect. The subject "products" is plural, so the verb "are" (plural) should be used instead of "is" (singular) to maintain subject-verb agreement. The correct sentence is: The products we source from them are not connected to the livestock industry.

Option (d) is also incorrect. The error is related to the subject-verb agreement issue. The plural verb "take" is incorrect. The subject "It" is singular, so the verb should also be singular. The correct form should be "takes" (singular) to agree with the singular subject "It." The correct sentence is: It takes courage to open yourself up to scrutiny again. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Arush have been a member of the club since its inception.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'Arush have been'. The error is related to subject-verb agreement. "Arush" is a singular noun, so it should be followed by the singular verb "has," not the plural "have." Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Arush has been a member of the club since its inception.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Neither the manager nor the assistant manager were available when the client arrived for the meeting.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'were available when the'. The error is related to subject-verb agreement. The subject of the sentence is "Neither the manager nor the assistant manager." This is a compound subject connected to "neither...nor." When using "neither...nor," the verb should agree with the closer subject in terms of proximity. In this case, "assistant manager" is closer to the verb. "Assistant manager" is a singular subject, so the verb should be singular as well. The correct verb form to use with a singular subject is "was" [singular] not "were" [plural]. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Neither the manager nor the assistant manager was available when the client arrived for the meeting.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Every students must submit the assignment by Friday.
Every students must submits the assignment by Friday.
Every student must submit the assignment by Friday.
Every student must submits the assignment by Friday.
questions.solution:
The sentence given in option (c) is grammatically correct.

Options (a) and (b) are incorrect because the subject "students" is plural, but the determiner "every" requires a singular noun ("student") in place of the plural noun 'students'. The determiner "every" is used with a singular noun.

Option (d) is also incorrect. After the modal verb "must", we use the base form of the verb. But 'submits' [third person singular verb] is not the base form. So, 'submits' should be replaced with the base form 'submit'. Option (b) also contains this error. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Every student must submit the assignment by Friday.

NOTE:

Determiner: A modifying word that determines the kind of reference a noun or noun group has, for example, 'a', 'the', 'every', 'much', 'many', etc.

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A) Rohini have been working on this project for two weeks. She needs to complete the final report in the next 10 days.

B) Rohini has been working on this project for two weeks. She needs to complete the final report in the next 10 days.

C) Rohini have been working on this project for two weeks. She need to complete the final report in the next 10 days.

D) Rohini has been working on this project for two weeks. She need to complete the final report in the next 10 days.
questions.solution:
The grammatically correct sentence is B. The error in sentence A is in the subject-verb agreement. "Rohini" is a singular subject, so the verb should be singular ("has") instead of the plural "have." The error in sentence C is again related to subject-verb agreement. "Have" [plural] should be replaced with the singular "has" to agree with the singular subject "Rohini." Additionally, "need" (plural) should be replaced with the singular "needs" to match the singular subject "She." The error in sentence D is in the subject-verb agreement. "She" (a singular subject) requires "needs" (singular) instead of the plural "need." Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.question:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with one blank, followed by four options, each having a word which may or may not fit in the blank. From the given options, choose the one that gives the correct word that fits in the blank.

His father and mentor _____ arrived on time.
questions.solution:
When the subjects suggest one idea to the mind or refer to the same person or thing, the verb is singular. So, options (a) and (d) are negated. In an active voice sentence 'is' is always followed by a verb in continuous form. Since the verb 'arrived' is in past participle form, option (c) is also negated. Only option (b), 'has' fits the sentence grammatically.

The correct sentence is: His father and mentor has arrived on time.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with one blank, followed by four options, each having a word which may or may not fit in the blank. From the given options, choose the one that gives the correct word that fits in the blank.

The monitor and the keyboard _____ broken by him yesterday.
questions.solution:
When the two singular nouns in a sentence refer to different persons or things, the article 'the' is used before each noun. In such cases, the verb will be plural. Accordingly, options (a) and (b) are negated. Option (c), 'are' is a present tense verb but the sentence is in Past tense. So, it is also negated. Only option (d), 'were' grammatically fits the blank.

The correct sentence is: The monitor and the keyboard were broken by him yesterday.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with one blank, followed by four options, each having a word which may or may not fit in the blank. From the given options, choose the one that gives the correct word that fits in the blank.

The row of chairs _____ arranged by him, today.
questions.solution:
A verb must agree in number and person with its subject and not just the nearest noun or the complement. Accordingly, the noun 'row' (singular) is the subject and the verb must be singular too. So, options (b), (c) and (d) are negated and 'today' denotes present tense. Option (a), 'is' is the most appropriate verb to fill the blank.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given with a phrase highlighted in bold. Select the option given below that can replace the phrase in bold to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct and mark that as your answer. If the sentence is correct as it is mark 'No correction required', as the answer.

Every student and every teacher are working hard to improve the results.
questions.solution:
When two nouns are qualified by each or every, even though connected by 'and', they take a singular verb. So, 'are working' is grammatically incorrect because it is a plural verb.

Among the given options, 'is working' is the only correct choice.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Every student and every teacher is working hard to improve the results.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

More than one train have (A)/ been delayed due to (B)/ fog today, so you might (C)/ have to wait a little bit.
questions.solution:
Part A has an error. The phrases like 'more than one', 'many a' are singular in form but plural in meaning and take up singular verbs. So, 'have' should be replaced by 'has' in order to rectify the error. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The final correct sentence would be: More than one train has been delayed due to fog today, so you might have to wait a little bit.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

Anna or her sisters (A)/ feeds the street dogs(B)/ every night after (C)/ their mother sleeps(D).
questions.solution:
Part B has an error. If a sentence contains a compound subject connected by 'or', the verb must agree with the subject nearer to it. The subject nearer to the verb is plural, so the verb should also be a plural. We need to replace 'feeds' by 'feed'. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The final correct sentence would be: Anna or her sisters feed the street dogs every night after their mother sleeps.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

Neither my sister(A)/ nor I thinks that David(B)/ could do such a(C)/ horrible thing as a murder(D).
questions.solution:
Part B has an error. If a compound subject is joined with the words 'either/or 'neither/nor), the verb must agree with the subject that is closer to the verb. 'I' is closer to the verb, so 'thinks' will be replaced by 'think'. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The final sentence would be: Neither my sister nor I think that David could do such a horrible thing as a murder.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

Each of you have(A) your own keys to the locker(B), so there's no need(C) to quarrel over this(D).
questions.solution:
Part A has an error. When the subject of the sentence is referred to with 'each', it takes the verb as singular. So, have' should be replaced by 'has'. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The final sentence would be: Each of you has your own keys to the locker, so there's no need to quarrel over this.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

A number of activities (A)/ including the sale of essential goods is (B)/ relaxed during the (C)/ lockdown period by the government. (D)
questions.solution:
Part B has an error.

The phrase 'a number of' takes a plural noun and a plural verb after it. The phrase, 'the number of' takes a plural noun but a singular verb after it.

Therefore, in the given sentence, the singular auxiliary verb 'is' should be replaced with its plural form 'are' to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: A number of activities including the sale of essential goods are relaxed during the lockdown period by the government.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

Some money from the parents' (A)/ accounts are spent by (B)/ the 17-year-old to buy (C)/ in-game cosmetic items and virtual ammunition. (D)
questions.solution:
Part B has an error.

When any of 'some, any, none, all, more / most, is used with a countable noun, the verb is plural and when any of these is used with an uncountable noun, the verb is singular. Since the noun 'money' is an uncountable noun, the verb 'are' should be replaced with its singular form 'is' to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Some money from the parents' accounts is spent by the 17-year-old to buy in-game cosmetic items and virtual ammunition.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer.

Not only the students but also (A)/ the coach have convinced the (B)/ management that they should only (C)/ reveal the name next week. (D)
questions.solution:
Part B has an error.

When not only..but also combines two subjects, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. So, the auxiliary verb 'have' should be replaced with its singular form 'has' to justify the singular subject 'coach'.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Not only the students but also the coach has convinced the management that they should only reveal the name next week.
